clue.text: Like the impertinence of hitmaker?

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of similar to
sass is cheeky talk or impertinence
in can stand for of, as in 'one in ten' for 'one of ten'

explanation.surface: A question about whether a pop hitmaker is famously cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitmaker' suggests a chart-topping musician, but here it is someone who carries out hits, that is, contract killings.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a hired killer, one who makes a hit in criminal slang.

clue.text: A payment in advance will secure choice

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sub is an advance payment on wages
per means a, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: Paying in advance guarantees a choice item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like an article but is the piece: PER, as in 'ten pounds a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Choice as an adjective means of top quality, which is what superb means.

clue.text: Inclusive of current core representatives of theatre, films, music and fiction?

definitions.text: Inclusive of current core representatives of theatre, films, music and fiction?

indicators.note: inclusive of means containing, so the central letters hold the extra one
core means the centre, so the middle letter of each word is taken

parts.note: its middle letter is A
its middle letter is L
its middle letter is S
its middle letter is T
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A question about who represents the arts today.
explanation.walkthrough: The middles of theatre, films, music and fiction are A, L, S, T; they include I. The whole clue also describes top celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the top tier of celebrities, the leading figures of the arts.

clue.text: Ruffled, glamourpuss not so sweet

indicators.note: ruffled means disturbed, so the letters are mixed up
not tells us the letters of so are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A dishevelled glamourpuss is not so sweet after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like it describes the glamourpuss, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugarplum is a small round confection, a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Memos lawyer returning from sunless vacation?

indicators.note: the lawyer comes back from the holiday, so that piece follows it

parts.note: a holiday with no sun gives you no tan
a DA is an American district attorney

explanation.surface: A lawyer back from a sunless holiday writes memos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacation' is the American word for holiday, pointing to an American lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Notanda is Latin for things to be noted, so it means memos or notes.

clue.text: Vatican City's No.1 missed playing forward!

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moving about freely, so they are rearranged
missed tells us the named letter is left out of the word Vatican
No.1 picks out the first letter of the word City's

parts.note: its first letter is C

explanation.surface: A cry about the Vatican's top figure missing as his team pushes forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing C from VATICAN leaves VATIAN, which 'playing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Avanti is the Italian exclamation urging people onward, a fitting cry in an Italian setting.

clue.text: Like a jolly loud warning?

parts.note: a la, French for in the style of, means like
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is like a cheerful loud warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective, but it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a loud signal that warns of danger.

clue.text: No help, sadly, given by service to a Swiss summoner

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: No help is given to a Swiss summoner by the service.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'Swiss summoner' does double work: it opens the answer as well as reading naturally before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenhorn is a long wooden horn once used to call cattle and signal across Alpine valleys.

clue.text: Thematically shaped tiles are put up around second base

indicators.note: around means the pieces sit either side of the letter for second
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to set is to put
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Tiles are stacked around second base on a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' is E, the base of natural logarithms. 'Thematically' points to the puzzle's theme of squares: these tiles are square.
explanation.definitionFit: Tesserae are the small square pieces of stone or glass used in mosaics.

clue.text: Start betting cartel

parts.note: SP is the starting price in horse-race betting
a ring is a group of traders fixing prices, a cartel

explanation.surface: A betting cartel gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to leap up suddenly, which is to start in the sense of jumping in surprise.

clue.text: Contemplative beer producer, Italian, takes soft drink, preposterously

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a trat (short for trattoria) is an Italian restaurant
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: preposterous literally means back-to-front, so the word for drink is read the other way

parts.note: to sip is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: An Italian brewer of contemplative bent orders a soft drink, absurdly.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAT takes in (holds) P and PIS, which is SIP read backwards because of 'preposterously'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappists are a silent, contemplative order of monks, and several Trappist abbeys brew famous beers.

clue.text: High point for Scot, commandeering Rolls to carry off the relations

indicators.note: commandeering means taking over and holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain peak

indicators.note: to carry means to hold within, so the letters sit inside

parts.note: RR is short for Rolls-Royce

indicators.note: off suggests the word the is knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish summit, a Rolls-Royce hijacked, and family members carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges THE to ETH; RR carries it to make RETHR, which BEN then takes over.
explanation.definitionFit: Brethren is the old plural of brother, used for kinsmen or fellow members, that is, relations.

clue.text: "Bust" is me with no cash

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the following words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with no money laments that they are bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Monies is a formal plural for sums of money, so it stands in for cash.

clue.text: What Santa is fundamentally right to take in his employee program Shape? Pride

indicators.note: to take in means to hold inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: the first letter, the foundation, of Santa is S
Santa's employee is an elf
an app is a computer program
an oval is a shape

explanation.surface: Santa takes on his elf helpers with a new programme, and the result is a shape of pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What Santa is fundamentally' means the letter Santa is founded on, its first, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-approval is satisfaction with oneself, a form of pride.

clue.text: Upper and lower parts of this grid are shot

definitions.text: Upper and lower parts of this grid are
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the top and bottom halves of the finished grid carry hidden words, so they are, literally
second meaning: a cricket stroke hit square of the wicket on the off side

explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle hides a pattern in the grid on the theme of squares and the central row splits the grid; the second sense is from cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the square cut is a batting stroke played across the line of an off-side ball.

clue.text: Suffering first of blows during remarkable game

parts.note: pain is suffering

indicators.note: during means within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: tall, as in a tall story, means hard to believe, remarkable

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of blows

explanation.surface: Suffering the first blows during a remarkable game.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintball is a combat sport in which players shoot each other with capsules of paint.

clue.text: Ace in clothes for soaring over the Med?

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
soaring means rising, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

parts.note: enrobes means dresses, clothes as a verb
A is short for ace in cards

explanation.surface: An ace pilot in flying gear soars over the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb, ENROBES; read upwards it gives SEBORNE, and A goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaborne means carried on or across the sea, such as the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Modified proposal connected to torpedo assignment?

parts.note: re means concerning, connected to
a sub, or submarine, is the vessel that fires torpedoes
a mission is an assigned task

explanation.surface: A revised plan linked to a naval torpedo job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torpedo assignment' reads as SUB MISSION, the job of a torpedo-firing submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A resubmission is a proposal sent in again, usually after being revised.

clue.text: Effected dispersal of clouds so was quick to catch some sun

indicators.note: to catch means to grab and hold, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: sped means went fast, was quick
a ray is a beam, a little bit of sunshine

explanation.surface: Someone dispersed the clouds and hurried to catch some sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To spray is to scatter a liquid in fine droplets, sending out clouds of it.

clue.text: Marauding king landed, it's appreciated, from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: alit is a past tense of alight, to land
ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: A raiding king lands, and that is appreciated, coming up from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila was king of the Huns, notorious for his raids across the Roman Empire.

clue.text: See teetotaller, naked, moon

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: a sober one is someone who does not drink

explanation.surface: An instruction to see a naked teetotaller mooning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moon' looks like a verb about baring a bottom, but it is the definition: a moon of a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is one of the moons of Uranus, named after the fairy king.

clue.text: Certainly not dispensing with refreshment for the afternoon occasion

indicators.note: dispensing with means doing without, so the drink is removed

parts.note: no chance is an emphatic way of saying certainly not
cha is a slang word for tea, the afternoon refreshment

explanation.surface: No tea for the afternoon do, certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: The British have tea in the afternoon; cha is a slang name for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The nonce is the present occasion, as in the phrase for the nonce.

clue.text: Restrained tango breaks hectic routine

indicators.note: breaks into means enters, so one letter goes inside the rest
hectic suggests frantic disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancer's restrained tango interrupts a hectic routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hectic' rearranges ROUTINE to RIENUTO, and T breaks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritenuto is a musical direction meaning held back, an immediate slowing of tempo.

clue.text: A kid's character not even the Empire State will embrace

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold around, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: New York, abbreviated NY, is nicknamed the Empire State
odd numbers are not even

explanation.surface: New York will embrace a strange children's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddy is the little wooden toy hero of Enid Blyton's children's books.

clue.text: Tin drum collected spiritlessly by the military escort

indicators.note: collected means gathered in, so the pieces go inside
by here completes collected by, marking the army as the container

parts.note: the army is the military
a can is a tin

indicators.note: spiritlessly means without spirit, so the spirit rum is taken out of drum

parts.note: drum, taken as written, loses its spirit
rum is the spirit removed, leaving just D

explanation.surface: Soldiers gather a tin drum listlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiritlessly' strips the spirit rum from drum, leaving only D.
explanation.definitionFit: Arm candy is a glamorous companion worn on the arm at events, an escort for show.

clue.text: Missing the first ordinal out, the second of twelve

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
missing the first means the opening letter of ordinal is dropped

explanation.surface: A puzzle about ordinal numbers: dropping the first leaves the second of twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the second of twelve' sounds like a numbering exercise; it means the second of the twelve men who walked on the Moon. ORDINAL without O leaves RDINAL, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Buzz Aldrin followed Neil Armstrong onto the lunar surface, the second of twelve moonwalkers.

clue.text: Someone must pay her new girl support

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a girl newly introduced to society
a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Someone must pay the new girl her support.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtee is a creditor, the person to whom money is owed.

clue.text: Aussie carrier: attendant, ill, switches wings

indicators.note: switches means the letters at the two ends trade places

parts.note: a gilly or ghillie is an attendant on a Scottish hunting or fishing trip
the G at the front of gilly is swapped out
D, the end of bad, comes in at the front

indicators.note: the wings are the outer letters, which are the ones swapped

parts.note: bad means ill

explanation.surface: An Australian bag-carrier who is an attendant falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: GILLY + BAD gives GILLYBAD; switching its outer letters G and D gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilly bag is an Australian Aboriginal mesh bag for carrying food and belongings.
